content: The effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives may be diminished when used concurrently with enzyme inducers, such as rifapentine, due to increased metabolism mediated by hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4. It is recommended to use an alternative or backup method of contraception during co-administration and to continue backup contraception for 28 days after discontinuing the enzyme inducer to ensure contraceptive reliability. Rifapentine reduces the plasma levels and therapeutic effects of linagliptin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and alternative treatments are strongly recommended when linagliptin is co-administered with CYP3A4 inducers. Rifapentine decreases the levels and efficacy of lomitapide, lopinavir, loratadine, losartan, maraviroc, marijuana, medroxyprogesterone, mefloquine, mestranol, methadone, methylprednisolone, metoprolol, midazolam, mifepristone, mirtazapine, modafinil, nateglinide, nelfinavir, nevirapine, nicardipine, nifedipine, nilotinib, nisoldipine, norgestrel, oliceridine, osilodrostat, ospemifene, oxycodone, paclitaxel, parecoxib, pazopanib, phenytoin, pimavanserin, pitolisant, polatuzumab vedotin, prednisolone, prednisone, primaquine, propranolol, quazepam, quetiapine, quinidine, repaglinide, ribociclib, rifabutin, riociguat, ritonavir, ruxolitinib, selexipag, sildenafil, sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid, solifenacin, sorafenib, sufentanil, sunitinib, suvorexant, tacrolimus, tadalafil, tamoxifen, tamsulosin, tasimelteon, temsirolimus, teniposide, terbinafine, tetracycline, theophylline, tiagabine, ticagrelor, tinidazole, tipranavir, tofacitinib, tolterodine, toremifene, tramadol, triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension, triazolam, vardenafil, verapamil, and vilazodone by enhancing their metabolism through CYP3A4 or other hepatic enzymes. For all these drugs, caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. In some cases, therapy modification, dose adjustments, or alternative treatments may be required. For drugs with significant therapeutic implications, such as hormonal contraceptives, opioids, or antiretrovirals, additional precautions, including the use of backup methods or avoidance of co-administration, may be necessary.
